analysis: Examined provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift head lines 1-1022. The only change (head 566-569, range map complete) adds two actor-isolated stored properties: clusterUpdateDrainID (String?) and clusterUpdateDrainTask (Task<Void, Never>?). These record a cluster-member coordinated-update drain that owns admission, implemented in ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain, which is not supplied here. The declarations alone add no wire parsing, crypto, attestation or authorization logic. They do not touch keyPair, signer, modelHashes or prefix-cache state (T-041, A-003, TB-011). No regression is visible in this unit. Questions for integration, all about the unseen extension file: (1) Can a coordinator message or any other party set clusterUpdateDrainID, and does an adversarial provider-side peer or pair member have any role? (2) Does the drain correctly gate admission alongside updatePhase, servingDrain, lifecycleDrain, addon holds and isShuttingDown? (3) Is clusterUpdateDrainTask cancelled on shutdown, disconnect and memberControlRequiresStop? A leaked task could hold admission closed indefinitely, an availability concern for A-018. (4) Is the drain ID matched to the request id that opened it, so a stale or foreign release cannot reopen admission mid-update (T-053-style stale state)? These questions affect availability, not confidentiality; they need the extension source to answer.
